summary: The note argues that sportsmanship is the core value of amateur sports teams, shaping community bonds, personal growth, inclusivity, education and ethics. It illustrates this with examples from local teams such as the Riverside Runners, Hillside Hawks, Mavericks and Sunnydale Strikers, plus quotes from players and coaches. Amateur sports are presented as vehicles for moral education and societal harmony.
one_line: Amateur sports teams foster community, personal growth, inclusivity, academic benefits and ethical decision-making through sportsmanship, illustrated by local team anecdotes.
key_facts: On September 5, 2023, the local amateur soccer league was in full swing in a city park, with teams made up of teachers, students, accountants and stay-at-home parents.
Midtown Mavericks, Riverside Runners and Hillside Hawks are named as staple amateur teams in their communities.
Clara Jenkins is the coach of the Hillside Hawks, and Jamal Richardson is a Mavericks stalwart who manages as a volunteer.
On September 15, 2023, Riverside Runners captain Michael Santorini allowed an unhindered substitution after a key opposing player was injured, an act not mandated by any rulebook.
Both teams in the September 15 match were lauded by the community for upholding the spirit of the game.
Maria Gonzalez, a single mother, found solace and strength joining the Mavericks and said on October 10, 2023 that it is 'about lifting each other up.'
The multicultural fabric of the Hillside Hawks was on display during the annual community cup in late September.
Clara Jenkins said, 'Here, we play as one. It doesn't matter where you come from or what you believe in.'
Jonathan Lee, a high school teacher and junior amateur basketball league coach, said on November 12, 2023 that students in sports tend to perform better academically.
On October 19, 2023, the youth soccer team Sunnydale Strikers forfeited a game after realizing an administrative error let an ineligible player play in their previous match.
The Sunnydale Strikers' forfeit cost them their place in the league championships.
The note says players develop resilience, empathy and leadership, and that sports build discipline, focus and collaboration skills.
